Theme

Latin word

nisi

conjunction; the word excepted keeps the case of the word it is taken from

except, but (after a negative: nothing but, no one but); unless, if not

In this lexicon

  • except

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 123.1: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē; Quint. 6 pr. 14: nēmō nisi suā culpā diū dolet

  • unless

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 21: crēdō, nisi eam exerceās; Cic. Tusc. 4.78: quō tē modō, inquit, accēpissem, nisi īrātus essem!; Traupman 311

  • nisi fallor: probably

    classical

  • Dē mortuīs nīl nisi bonum.: speak no ill of the dead

    modern

  • nisi molestum est: trouble

    classical

Examples

  • itinere cōnfectus incommodō magis quam longō in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē

    worn out by a journey more awkward than long, I reached my house at Alba late at night: nothing is ready except meSen. Ep. 123.1

    In the entry for except

  • tōta mihi dormītur hiems et pinguior illō tempore sum quō mē nīl nisi somnus alit

    I sleep the whole winter through, and I am fattest at the time when nothing but sleep feeds meMart. 13.59.1–2

    In the entry for except

  • nūlla jam ultrā gēns, nihil nisi flūctūs et saxa

    there is no people beyond us now, nothing but waves and rocksTac. Agr. 30.5

    In the entry for except

  • at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās

    but memory fades. — I dare say, unless you exercise itCic. Sen. 21

    In the entry for unless

    In the entry for unless

    if I didn’t love you more than my own eyesCatull. 14.1

    nothing (is different), except that the midday nap is droppedPlin. Ep. 9.40.2
